title: Heterogeneous tool fanout with idempotent merge and cycle detection
creator: Aisha Tan
description: Design and implement a robust execution protocol for multi-tool fanout where heterogeneous tools (sync API calls, streaming model calls, and long-running jobs) can be invoked within the same user session. The goal is a safe, observable, and compatible tool execution loop that: (1) merges results idempotently from parallel tools, (2) prevents infinite recursion / loops from model-triggered tool chains, (3) supports streaming partial results and function-calling structured outputs, and (4) remains compatible with existing Redwood Runtime APIs and the compatibility layer for older SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic merge strategy is implemented such that repeated tool responses (retries or replays) do not corrupt the session state
Cycle detection stops runaway tool-chaining after configurable thresholds and logs a clear provenance record
Streaming results from any fanout branch are delivered to the client in order with backpressure signals for slow consumers
Tool outputs include signed provenance metadata that the orchestrator uses when injecting results into the LLM prompt or state
Compatibility layer gracefully accepts older SDKs that send tool requests without explicit session IDs and maps them to quarantined sessions
Comprehensive unit + integration tests that simulate heterogeneous fanout (model->tool->model->tool) and validate idempotency and halt behavior
notes: Motivation: customers are composing multiple helper functions and external services at runtime (embeddings search + reranker + external db write + webhook) and have reported inconsistent merges and dangling loops under retries
Trade-offs considered: conservative serial execution simplifies reasoning but increases latency; optimistic parallel fanout reduces latency but requires stronger merge and cycle policies

Related designs: Runtime streaming protocol v2 (design doc link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runtime/streaming-v2), session quarantine RFC (drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/priv/session-quarantine.pdf)
Security: tool result provenance must be tamper-evident to prevent injected instructions from external tools; consider HMAC over (tool_id, session_id, seq) with key stored in KMS
Monitoring: add metrics for 'fanout_depth', 'fanout_success_rate', 'cycle_aborts', and sampling traces for complex sessions
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Design protocol messages for fanout branches including session_id, branch_id, parent_branch_id, deterministic operation_id
Phase 2: Implement idempotent merge: each branch writes a stable result token; orchestrator merges by priority rules (schema-aware) and rejects duplicate tokens
Phase 3: Add cycle detection engine: maintain per-session invocation DAG up to depth N, enforce deadman timer and abort/circuit state
Phase 4: Streaming integration: adapt existing streaming layer to multiplex branch frames (FRAME: metadata + payload + provenance signature) and backpressure tokens
Phase 5: Compatibility shims: accept legacy calls without branch metadata by creating a quarantined wrapper branch with synthetic ids
Phase 6: Tests + canary rollout on a subset of runtime pools; observe cost/latency tradeoffs and iterate
tests: Unit: deterministic merge logic with duplicate, out-of-order, and partial payloads
Integration: simulated fanout with mix of local tools, external webhooks, and model streaming endpoints
Fault injection: tool crashes mid-stream, tooling timeouts, HMAC mismatch on provenance
Load: parallel sessions with deep fanout to measure latency impact and memory/KV cache pressure
Compatibility: legacy SDK calls mapped into quarantine mode and validated end-to-end
dependencies: ENG-8421 (tool-runner deterministic chaining) - reuse id generation pattern
ENG-47253 (sandboxed-executor stream-aware guardrails) - coordinate stream multiplexing
infra/kms-integration (internal infra ticket) - provisioning for provenance keys
sdk-compat-layer (pm/pm ticket) - spec for legacy client behavior mapping
